# SEO audit: acme-invoice.example (pre-launch preview)
2026-09-29 · Scope: the preview at `http://127.0.0.1:8799`, which goes live at `https://acme-invoice.example`. All 9 sitemap URLs, plus `/app`, `/admin/` and 404 handling. Priority pages: `/pricing`, `/features/invoicing`, `/blog/how-to-write-an-invoice`. Missing HTTPS is ignored because this is a local preview. · Data: 10 pages crawled plus all 9 sitemap URLs checked. GSC: yes, but from the **old** domain (Queries + Pages; the export doesn't record its date range). Keyword/SERP tool: no. PageSpeed: no.

## Executive summary
- **Overall:** crawling, rendering and mobile setup are fine: the HTML is server-rendered, has no JS dependency and has a viewport tag on every page. Two of the three priority pages have clean head tags. The content is not ready to launch, though. `/pricing` shows no plans or prices, and 7 of 9 pages repeat the same 186-word filler paragraph.
- **Biggest risk: the domain move.** In the export, the old site's top 3 URLs earned **1,430 clicks and 36,000 impressions**. No redirect plan exists yet. The old post URL `/blog/write-invoice` (6,000 impressions) returns a 200 "Page not found" on the new site. `/templates`, the old site's best page (900 clicks, position 2.1), has no downloadable templates in its HTML.
- **Biggest opportunity:** "invoice software" gets 12,000 impressions at position 4.2 but only a **0.33% CTR**. That's about 860 missed clicks, part of about 1,500 missed clicks on the homepage. "How to write an invoice" sits on page 2 (position 13.4, 5,000 impressions) with a post that currently has about 37 words of real content.
- **Unknown:** Core Web Vitals (PageSpeed can't reach localhost), SERPs, "People also ask", competitor keywords and backlinks. The keyword tool and web search weren't available in this session. The target country is also unknown: the copy spells "itemised" (UK), and the export has no Countries sheet.
- **This week:** build the old-to-new 301 redirect map, make unknown URLs return a real 404, and verify a GSC Domain property for `acme-invoice.example` by DNS **before** launch.

## Findings by section

### Technical
- ❌ **T3 Indexing issues**: unknown URLs return **200** with the title "Page not found" (a soft 404). Tested: `/this-page-does-not-exist-xyz`, `/blog/write-invoice`, `/about`, `/blog`, `/pricing/`, `/Pricing`, `/features`, `/index.html`. The sitemap also lists `/legacy`, which is `noindex`. **Do:** send the friendly not-found page with a `404` status. Remove `/legacy` from `sitemap-pages.xml`. After launch, check GSC > Pages for "Soft 404" and "Excluded by noindex".
- ❌ **T9 Broken links, 404s, redirect chains**:
  - The homepage links to `/features/reports`, which returns **404**.
  - The blog post links to `/old-pricing`, which goes 301 → `/pricing-2023` → 301 → `/pricing` (2 hops). The anchor text also reads "Old link: see our pricing".
  - `/app` (the "Log in" link on every page) answers **302 to itself** with `Set-Cookie: session=1`. Googlebot doesn't keep cookies, so it sees an endless loop.
  - The old domain has no redirects to the new one (see T3 and the redirect map).

  **Do:**
  - Build `/features/reports` or remove the link.
  - Change the blog link to `<a href="/pricing">see Acme Invoice pricing</a>`.
  - Make `/app` return 200 on the first request and set the cookie on that response.
  - Ship the [redirect map](#redirect-map-ready-to-paste).
- ❌ **T5 Canonicals**:
  - `/pricing` has no canonical, and `/pricing?utm_source=x` serves the same page with a 200.
  - The not-found template outputs the literal `href="{origin}/"`.
  - Canonicals, sitemap `<loc>` entries and the robots.txt `Sitemap:` line all follow the request `Host` header. Sending `Host: staging.other-host.test` produced `<link rel="canonical" href="http://staging.other-host.test/features/invoicing">`, so a staging host, a `www` variant or a proxy hostname would leak into production canonicals.

  The other 7 indexable pages have a correct self-referencing canonical. **Do:** build every absolute URL from a config constant, `SITE_URL = "https://acme-invoice.example"`, and add `<link rel="canonical" href="https://acme-invoice.example/pricing">` to `/pricing`.
- ❌ **T1 GSC & GA4**: you've confirmed there's no GSC property on the new domain. None of the 10 pages has a `gtag.js`, GTM or other analytics script. **Do:** add a **Domain** property for `acme-invoice.example` with a DNS TXT record now; this works before launch. Keep the old property verified, since Change of Address needs both. Install GA4 (or your analytics) and link it to GSC.
- ❌ **T11 Breadcrumbs**: no inner page shows a visible breadcrumb. `/features/invoicing` has `BreadcrumbList` with `"itemListElement":[]`, which fails validation. `/pricing` and the blog post have none. **Do:** add a visible trail (`Home › Blog › How to write an invoice`, `Home › Invoicing`) with matching JSON-LD ([snippet](#schema-ready-to-paste)).
- ❌ **T13 Schema**:
  - The homepage `Organization` has `"url":"/"` (relative) and no `logo` or `sameAs`.
  - `BreadcrumbList` is empty (see T11).
  - `BlogPosting` has no `dateModified`, `image`, `publisher` or `author.url`.
  - `/pricing`, `/templates` and `/blog/` have no JSON-LD at all.

  **Do:** paste the [schema below](#schema-ready-to-paste), then test each template in the Rich Results Test once the site is live.
- ⚠️ **T2 Sitemaps**: `robots.txt` points to `/sitemap_index.xml`, which lists `sitemap-pages.xml` and `sitemap-blog.xml.gz` (9 URLs). That's good. But the sitemap includes `/legacy` (noindex), every `<lastmod>` is the same `2026-09-01`, and the URLs come from the `Host` header (see T5). **Do:** remove `/legacy`, set `lastmod` from each page's real last edit, and generate URLs from `SITE_URL`. Submit `https://acme-invoice.example/sitemap_index.xml` in GSC and in Bing Webmaster Tools (use "Import from GSC") on launch day.
- ⚠️ **T4 robots.txt / noindex**: robots.txt only blocks `/admin/`, and nothing important is blocked. However, `/admin/` is linked from the nav on every page and carries `noindex`. Because crawling it is disallowed, Google never sees that `noindex` and can still index the bare URL. **Do:** remove "Admin" from the public nav and put `/admin/` behind authentication (401 or a redirect to login).
- ⚠️ **T12 Orphan pages**: `/orphan-landing` ("Invoicing Software for Photographers") is in the sitemap but has no internal links. `/legacy` is also unlinked, which is fine because it's noindex. **Do:** link the photographers page from the homepage (a "Who it's for" block) and from `/features/invoicing`, after renaming it (T10).
- ⚠️ **T10 URLs**:
  - `/orphan-landing` doesn't describe the page.
  - `/pricing/` and `/Pricing` return soft 404s instead of redirecting.
  - `/blog/` is the only URL with a trailing slash.

  **Do:** 301 `/orphan-landing` → `/invoicing-for-photographers`. 301 trailing-slash and uppercase variants to the canonical URL.
- ❓ **T6 Core Web Vitals**: PageSpeed Insights can't reach localhost (the request also returned HTTP 429). Risk looks low: the pages are 0.8–2.3 KB of HTML with no CSS or JS. The one image has no `width`/`height`, which risks layout shift once the real hero ships. **Need:** a PageSpeed run on a public staging URL, or the GSC Core Web Vitals report about 28 days after launch.
- ✅ **T7 Mobile friendly**: every page has `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">` and nothing has a fixed width. Check tap-target spacing in the nav again with the production stylesheet at 375 px.
- ✅ **T8 JS crawlability**: all content and links are in the server HTML. The only `<script>` tags are JSON-LD.

## Redirect map ready to paste
Old domain (anonymised as `example.com` in the export) → new domain, page to page, one hop each:

| Old URL | New URL | Old-site traffic |
|---|---|---|
| `https://example.com/` | `https://acme-invoice.example/` | 500 clicks / 20,000 impr. |
| `https://example.com/templates` | `https://acme-invoice.example/templates` | 900 clicks / 10,000 impr. |
| `https://example.com/blog/write-invoice` | `https://acme-invoice.example/blog/how-to-write-an-invoice` | 30 clicks / 6,000 impr. |
| every other path | same path on the new domain (then 301 or 404 there) | not in export |

```nginx
# Old domain: keep it registered and its certificate valid for at least a year
server {
    server_name example.com www.example.com;
    location = /blog/write-invoice { return 301 https://acme-invoice.example/blog/how-to-write-an-invoice; }
    location / { return 301 https://acme-invoice.example$request_uri; }
}

# New domain: point legacy paths straight at the final URL
location = /blog/write-invoice          { return 301 /blog/how-to-write-an-invoice; }
location = /old-pricing                 { return 301 /pricing; }
location = /pricing-2023                { return 301 /pricing; }
location = /blog                        { return 301 /blog/; }
location = /blog/invoice-template-guide { return 301 /templates; }
location = /orphan-landing              { return 301 /invoicing-for-photographers; }
```
Use the same rules in your host's redirect config if you're not on nginx (Vercel `vercel.json`, Netlify `_redirects`, Next.js `redirects()`). **Need:** the old site's full URL list (a crawl, or GSC Pages with up to 1,000 rows), including the login URL behind "payly login", so that no URL falls through to a 404.

## Schema ready to paste
Homepage, replacing the current `Organization`:
```json
{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"Organization","name":"Acme Invoice","url":"https://acme-invoice.example/","logo":"https://acme-invoice.example/img/logo.png","sameAs":["<LinkedIn URL>","<X/Twitter URL>"]}
```
`/features/invoicing`, replacing the empty `BreadcrumbList`:
```json
{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"BreadcrumbList","itemListElement":[
 {"@type":"ListItem","position":1,"name":"Home","item":"https://acme-invoice.example/"},
 {"@type":"ListItem","position":2,"name":"Automated invoicing","item":"https://acme-invoice.example/features/invoicing"}]}
```
`/blog/how-to-write-an-invoice`, replacing the current `BlogPosting` (add a matching `BreadcrumbList`: Home › Blog › post):
```json
{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"BlogPosting","headline":"How to write an invoice","mainEntityOfPage":"https://acme-invoice.example/blog/how-to-write-an-invoice","image":"https://acme-invoice.example/img/how-to-write-an-invoice.png","datePublished":"2025-01-10","dateModified":"<date the rewrite goes live>","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Jane Doe","url":"https://acme-invoice.example/authors/jane-doe"},"publisher":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Acme Invoice","logo":{"@type":"ImageObject","url":"https://acme-invoice.example/img/logo.png"}}}
```
`/pricing`: add a `SoftwareApplication` with `"applicationCategory":"BusinessApplication"`, `"operatingSystem":"Web"` and one `Offer` per plan (`"price":"0"` for Free; set `priceCurrency` to your billing currency). Google only shows a software rich result once `aggregateRating` or `review` is present, so add those when you have genuine reviews.
